title: Coons reconstruction error as a term of the grid-map Newton relaxation (boundaries slide onto creases)
description:
Goal: patch boundaries of the quad layout should land on curvature features (ridges, valleys, necks) instead of splitting across them. Explicit crest-line detection (PATCH-11, CRAW-5) and hand-placed rings (CRAW-22/23/28) were looked at and rejected as the primary mechanism: the first is brittle on scans, the second is manual. This ticket adds the variational alternative: the Coons reconstruction error of every patch becomes a term of the energy the grid-map Newton relaxation minimizes, so boundaries slide onto the creases that make their patches representable by their boundaries alone.

Where it lives. Stage 11-14 of QuadLayoutEngine: GridMapAssembly builds the integer grid map and its DofSystem, NewtonSolverNode relaxes it, GridMapOptimizer assembles the symmetric Dirichlet energy per triangle from the seamless UV (reference) to the grid UV (variables) with SPH17's PSD Hessian, and NewtonRelaxation runs damped Newton over a once-factorized sparsity. Nothing in that stage sees 3D positions today. PatchGridExtraction inverts every lattice point of every patch through the relaxed map onto the surface, and CoonsReconstructionError (PATCH-16, geometry/mesh/data) already measures a 4-sided patch's vertices against the cubic Coons blend of its boundary.

The term. For each live patch P with lattice points x_ij (row-major grid, PatchGridExtraction.gridByPatchId) and boundary samples on its four sides, define the residual r_ij = x_ij - Coons_P(s_i, t_j) and the energy E_coons = w * sum over patches and interior lattice points of |r_ij|^2, normalised by the squared quad edge length so it is dimensionless like the Dirichlet term. Each lattice point is the inverse of the grid map at a fixed grid location: inside one triangle it is the barycentric combination of that triangle's three 3D corner positions, with barycentrics that are a function of the triangle's three grid UV slots. Differentiating r_ij with respect to those slots goes through the 2x2 inverse Jacobian of the triangle's grid map (the inverse-map derivative: d(bary)/d(uv) = -J^-1 applied per corner).

Making it fit the solver. The triangle containing a lattice point changes as the map moves, so the exact energy is only C0 and its Hessian sparsity is not fixed. Resolve this with an outer loop of frozen assignments: at the start of each Newton pass, invert the lattice once (the extraction code), record per lattice point its triangle, barycentrics and, for boundary samples, the same. Within a pass treat the assignment as fixed. Then r_ij is a smooth function of a bounded set of slots and the Gauss-Newton Hessian J^T J is PSD by construction, which the projected-Newton step requires.

Two stencil variants, implement in this order:
(1) Frozen-Coons variant (first, minimal). Within a pass hold the Coons surface Coons_P fixed at its pass-start value. Each residual then depends only on the three slots of its own triangle: the stencil equals the Dirichlet stencil, the upper-key set in GridMapOptimizer.buildSparsityPattern is unchanged, and the term drops into assembleInto (Hessian and negative gradient accumulation per worker) and into totalEnergy (line-search trial energy) with no change to maximumStep. Boundary lattice points (the sides) get no residual in this variant; the boundary moves because interior points near it want to lie on the frozen Coons surface, and the surface is re-fit between passes.
(2) Moving-Coons variant (second, only if (1) stalls). Include the Coons surface's dependence on its boundary samples: each residual also touches the triangles of the boundary samples it blends (the two side points at the same i and the two at the same j, plus the four corners). The stencil grows; extend the upper-key set at pattern-build time from the frozen assignment of the pass, which means the factorization handle is rebuilt once per pass, not per iteration.

Outer loop. relax -> re-extract lattice (PatchGridExtraction with optimizedGrid set) -> re-fit Coons per patch -> re-freeze -> relax, for a small fixed number of passes (start with 3) or until the summed Coons error stops dropping by more than 1 percent. GridMapDofSystem.relax is the natural driver; keep the single-pass behaviour when the weight is zero so nothing else changes.

Weight. Dirichlet at rest is 4 times the triangle's reference area. Start with w such that a residual of one quad edge length on a lattice point costs about the Dirichlet energy of the triangles that point's patch cell covers; expose it as a float input target on NewtonSolverNode (coons_weight, default 0 = off) so the scene can toggle it, and make the default of quad_layout's port the same 0 until verified.

Scope limits. This ticket moves existing boundaries by up to a few quad widths onto nearby creases. It does not create new boundaries; a ridge in the middle of a patch needs the Coons-error split operator on the T-mesh (separate ticket). It does not change the cross field; the leg-base diagonal field on fertility is a Hopf-guidance weighting issue (separate ticket). Singular nodes stay pinned; they are fixed points of their fan transitions.

Diagnostics to build first, before the energy term: a per-patch Coons-error colour overlay in the quad layout scene (dark = low, bright = high, reuse the PATCH-15 per-vertex scalar shader) computed from the initial and from the relaxed extraction, plus the summed and per-patch p95 error on the [grid-optimize] log line. This overlay is how the ticket is verified and how the claim "the patches that straddle ridges score high" is checked before the term is trusted.
definition-of-done:
1. A per-patch Coons reconstruction error is computed from the layout's extracted lattice (initial and relaxed) for every live 4-sided patch, and the quad layout scene shows it as a per-vertex scalar overlay with a key to toggle it; the [grid-optimize] log line reports summed Coons error and the worst patch before and after relaxation.
2. GridMapOptimizer carries an optional Coons-error term (frozen-Coons variant) with analytic gradient and Gauss-Newton PSD Hessian, assembled into the same sparsity as the Dirichlet term and included in the line-search trial energy; a finite-difference check of the gradient on a fixture passes to 1e-6 relative.
3. GridMapDofSystem.relax runs the frozen-assignment outer loop (re-extract, re-fit, relax) when the weight is positive and behaves exactly as before when it is zero; flippedTriangleCount stays 0 and the Dirichlet energy never becomes infinite.
4. NewtonSolverNode and quad_layout expose coons_weight (default 0); a fertility run with a positive weight reduces the summed Coons error and moves at least one patch boundary visibly toward a crease without raising the Dirichlet energy by more than a documented factor; before/after screenshots under tmp/ and the numbers on the ticket.
5. The launch.json entry for the scene exists and all unit tests pass; no VERIFICATION.md.
testing-plan:
1. Unit (fixture, no mesh): finite-difference check of the Coons term's gradient and of the inverse-map barycentric derivative on a hand-authored patch (PlaneLayoutFixture or a new small fixture) to 1e-6 relative; the Gauss-Newton block is symmetric PSD (eigenvalues >= -1e-12).
2. Unit: with coons_weight 0 the relaxation's energyAfter, iterationCount and worstVertexMove on the torus fixture are bit-identical to master.
3. Benchmark (deliberate, -Dtest=): fertility through buildGlobalGridMap with weight 0 and with the chosen positive weight; record summed Coons error, worst-patch p95, Dirichlet energyBefore/After, flipped=0, iterations, wall time; both numbers go on the ticket.
4. Scene: run the quad layout scene on fertility via ixdar-cli run-scene, toggle the Coons overlay, screenshot initial vs relaxed and weight-0 vs weight-on framed on the leg base and on one ridge-straddling patch; images under tmp/.
unknowns: Whether the frozen-Coons variant alone moves boundaries enough, or the moving-Coons stencil is needed; measure on fertility
Weight scale: the residual is a length, Dirichlet is dimensionless area-weighted distortion; the quad-edge normalisation is a first guess
Lattice points near a singular node lie in triangles with pinned corners; the term has no effect there, which is expected but should be visible in the overlay

Whether the Coons error should use the cubic Bezier side fit CoonsReconstructionError uses or the exact polyline sides from the extraction; exact sides are cheaper and match the Coons variant PatchSurfaceGeometry already renders

Frozen-Coons variant 1 helps but only by 14 percent on fertility, and it oscillates: the summed error goes 2.294e3 (pass 0) -> 1.896e3 (pass 1) -> 2.183e3 (pass 2). Moving the boundary moves the Coons surface the next pass re-fits, so the term chases its own target. Either damp the re-fit (blend the new surface with the previous one) or go to the moving-Coons stencil of variant 2 before calling the mechanism settled.

The term lowers the summed error but raises the worst patch's p95 (2.237 -> 2.779, and the worst patch changes from 176 to 150): it evens the error out rather than fixing the outliers. A max-style or p95-weighted term, or per-patch weights, is the obvious next experiment.

Weight scale: only w=10 was measured against w=0 on fertility; 1, 3 and 30 were not swept. w=10 makes the term about a third of the relaxed total energy and costs a factor 1.26 in Dirichlet. Whether a smaller weight gets most of the gain for less distortion is untested.

The re-inversion misses a handful of lattice sites once the map has moved (18 of 10191 by the third pass on fertility), which the fallback lattice papers over. The QEx path (QuadMeshExtraction/ExtractedPatchGrids) never misses; if the outer loop is ever run for more passes, extracting through that path mid-loop instead of PatchGridExtraction would be the sturdier fix.

Boundary lattice sites carry no residual in variant 1, so a patch boundary only moves because the interior points next to it pull. On fertility that was enough to shift boundaries by roughly a quad width; whether it reaches a crease two or three quads away is untested.

DIRECTION CHANGE (user, 2026-09-13): the goal is patch edges landing near creases, and the Coons term evens interior error out without pulling edges much. Next: replace/extend the frozen-Coons term with crease attraction on boundary lattice points: target = local maximum of CreaseField.bend within half a quad across the boundary, quadratic residual weighted by the maximum's strength, same frozen-assignment loop and triangle stencil.

The bend field is principal-curvature anisotropy, so thin tubes (arms) read uniformly bright, not only creases. The attraction term must use the local maximum of bend across the boundary within half a quad, weighted by how peaked it is, so a uniform tube exerts no pull; the absolute value would drag every edge toward thin limbs.

Smoothing radius of one quad edge is one mesh edge on fertility (a single Jacobi step); a floor of a few mesh edges may be needed on coarse meshes, and the radius should be re-checked on the crawfish scans where a quad spans many triangles.

The walk reach is tied to CreaseField.smoothingRadius, not to the ticket's half a quad edge: on fertility a quad edge is one mesh edge, so the specified window was half a mesh edge and the term was inert. The coupling is principled (a window narrower than the smoothing radius is flat by construction) but it means the crease term's range is now set by the smoothing radius floor, which was picked as 3 mesh edges by eye. Radius and reach should be swept together on the crawfish scans, where a quad spans many mesh edges and the two decouple.

The crease term buys boundary movement by spending Coons smoothness: summedCoons rises monotonically with crease_weight (2.49e3 at w=0 to 5.17e3 at w=30) and the worst patch's p95 with it (2.24 to 4.27). The two terms pull against each other and have never been run together (coons_weight and crease_weight both positive is untested). Whether a small Coons weight tidies the interiors the crease term distorts, or the two just fight, is the next experiment.

Weight 1 is slightly worse than weight 0 on the mean boundary-to-crease distance (3.241 against 3.183) while improving the p95. The target is recomputed each pass from the moved boundary, so a weak pull can leave a site chasing a target that has moved on; the same target-chasing the frozen-Coons variant showed. Damping the target between passes was not tried.

The re-extraction misses more boundary sites once the crease term has moved the map: unreached walk samples go from 0 before relaxation to about 4300-4700 of 27024 after, and 70-80 of 3378 sites lose their frozen triangle entirely. A site half whose walk leaves its own patch's rectangle simply gets a shorter walk; going through the QEx path, or admitting the chart neighbourhood into the walk, would recover them.
changes-made: Diagnostic first: PatchCoonsError (geometry/mesh/quadlayout/extraction) blends every live patch's four extracted grid borders and measures each interior lattice point against that blend, normalised by the mean 3D quad edge length. It reports the summed squared residual, the per-patch p95 and the worst patch. It runs on the pre-relaxation lattice (GridMapDofSystem.relax) and on the relaxed one (GridMapAssembly.extractQuads), both on [grid-optimize] log lines as coonsInitial / coonsRelaxed.

Resolved the open question on the Coons surface: the exact extracted polyline sides, not a cubic Bezier fit. PatchCoonsError.coonsBlend is the blend PatchSurfaceGeometry.coonsBundle already renders (CoonsEvaluator.blendGrid), so the two agree by construction, border sites score exactly zero and only interior sites enter the sums. PatchSurfaceGeometry's private duplicate of that blend was deleted in favour of the shared one.

Overlay: QuadLayoutScene key K paints the layout fill by the per-lattice-point residual instead of the patch hash colour, through the PATCH-15 mesh_scalar shader. QuadLayoutRuntime gained a second fill buffer (position + scalar at attribute 3, the location mesh_scalar.vs reads) and beginCoonsError, with a fixed ramp of 0..2 quad edges so two runs are comparable. Verified on fertility before trusting the term: ridge-straddling and cap patches are bright, flat cylindrical stretches dark.

Energy term (frozen-Coons variant 1): CoonsLatticeResidual (quadlayout/gridmap) is the element kernel. A lattice site is fixed in its triangle's chart, the triangle's three surface corners are fixed in space, so the variables are the corners' chart coordinates; the barycentric derivative d(lambda)/d(uv) is written out from the three sub-areas and the energy is w*|x_ij - Coons_P|^2 / quadEdgeLength^2 with the Gauss-Newton J^T J Hessian, PSD by construction.

The term rides the Dirichlet stencil exactly: a residual's three variables are its own triangle's, so buildSparsityPattern and upperKeys are untouched and the Coons gradient/Hessian are added into the SymmetricDirichletEnergy element before the one rotateElementToSlots and the one scatter. Residuals are held CSR by gathered triangle, so each worker's triangle range owns its residuals and the reduction stays deterministic. totalEnergy (the line-search trial energy) includes the term; maximumStep is unchanged.

Outer loop: GridMapDofSystem.relax runs up to 3 frozen-assignment passes (relax, re-extract the lattice through the moved map, re-fit the Coons surface, re-freeze) and stops early when the summed error drops by under 1 percent. coons_weight 0 takes the old single-pass path untouched.

Ports: NewtonSolverNode and quad_layout both expose coons_weight (FLOAT, default 0); QuadLayoutEngine.coonsWeight carries it into the solver node; QuadLayoutScene key J toggles it between 0 and 10 and rebuilds, which is how the before/after screenshots were taken (no system property).

PatchGridExtraction gained recordAssignment (per lattice site: source patch, its local triangle index and the site's coordinates in that patch's common-grid chart) and fallbackGrid. The fallback is needed because once the map has moved the depth-2 chart neighbourhood no longer reaches every site: on fertility 6/15/18 of 10191 sites over the three passes, which keep their previous position and carry no residual (unassigned=1 at most).

Fertility numbers (CoonsTermBenchmark, fertility_in_tri.off, alpha 15deg, 10191 interior lattice sites, quad edge 2.26 initial / 2.10 relaxed). weight 0: summedCoons 8.460e3 -> 2.493e3, worst-patch p95 7.036 -> 2.237 (patch 228 -> 176), Dirichlet 5.551e7 -> 4.020e4, 1 pass / 49 iterations, flipped 0, 19.1s. weight 10: summedCoons 8.460e3 -> 2.137e3 (14.3 percent below the weight-0 result), worst-patch p95 7.036 -> 2.779 (patch 228 -> 150), Dirichlet 5.551e7 -> 5.060e4 (a factor 1.26 above weight 0), 3 passes / 74 iterations, flipped 0, 19.4s. The grid-map stage is a small part of buildGlobalGridMap, so the extra passes cost no measurable wall time.

Tests: CoonsLatticeResidualTest (hand-authored fixture, no mesh) checks energyOnly against evaluate, the analytic gradient against central differences to 1e-6 relative through the inverse-map barycentric derivative, and the Gauss-Newton block symmetric PSD over 200 random configurations x 12 probe directions. GridMapOptimizerParallelTest gained weightZeroReproducesTheRecordedRelaxation, pinning the torus fixture's energyAfter (250747.0957407789), iterationCount (15) and worstVertexMove (3.0936609653315537) exactly, plus zero Coons residuals at weight 0. CoonsTermBenchmark (test/benchmark) is the fertility comparison. mvn test: Tests run: 226, Failures: 0, Errors: 0, Skipped: 0.

Crease field overlay (H key in quad-layout): CrossField.vertexBend stores the Hopf differential magnitude per vertex from NDirectionField.solveForHopfField; CreaseField (crossfield package) diffuses it over one quad edge (Jacobi neighbour averaging, steps = (radius/avgEdge)^2, capped 128) and reports mean/p95/max; the scene paints it through the SCALAR shader with the ramp at p95, hiding the patch fill so boundaries and quad grid draw over it. Verified on fertility: creases (base rim, necks, leg-base bulge, shoulder ridge) read as bright bands; screenshot tmp/patch-104-crease-field.png in the worktree.

Crease overlay screenshots at the agent's camera positions: tmp/patch-104-crease-legbase.png, tmp/patch-104-crease-ridge.png. On fertility the quad edge (2.13) is one average mesh edge, so the diffusion ran a single step (log: radius=2.095 (1.0 edges) steps=1 mean=0.1401 p95=0.4148 max=1.140).

Crease attraction term (the direction change): CreaseAttraction (quadlayout/extraction) takes every boundary lattice point of every live patch side once — arc sample points, deduped by (arcId, sample), node samples skipped — and walks the surface across the boundary from each. Both incident patches contribute one half of the walk in their own chart (inward from their own rectangle side), so no chart-neighbourhood machinery is needed and the two halves together straddle the boundary. Each walk sample is a chart point inverted through the patch's triangles; the bend is read by barycentric interpolation of CreaseField.bend, carried to the patch's dense vertices through each copy vertex's barycentric coordinate in its source face. Target p = the sample with the largest bend; peakedness q = (max - min along the walk) / CreaseField.rampMax clamped to [0,1]; transverse axis t = normalised difference of the two halves' innermost samples.

Residual: CoonsLatticeResidual gained a projectionAxis field. With it set, the residual vector and every column of the point Jacobian are replaced by their component along t, so the energy is w*((x-p).t)^2 and the Gauss-Newton block is 2w (t.J_i)(t.J_j) — rank one, PSD, same three-slot stencil and same sparsity as the Coons and Dirichlet terms, maximumStep untouched. No duplication: the barycentric-derivative code is the one that was already there. GridMapOptimizer's residual table was generalised to carry both terms — one CSR by gathered triangle with per-residual target, axis, weight and a projected flag — so Coons and crease residuals ride the same scatter, the same assembleInto and the same totalEnergy.

Outer loop and ports: GridMapDofSystem.relax runs the shared frozen-assignment passes (LATTICE_PASSES=3) when either weight is positive, recomputing the Coons surface and the crease targets from the re-extracted lattice each pass. Early exit on the Coons convergence test only applies when the crease term is off — the crease target moves with the boundary, so the Coons error is not its progress measure. crease_weight (FLOAT, default 0) on newton_solver and quad_layout; QuadLayoutEngine.creaseWeight carries it; GlobalGridMap.vertexBend feeds CreaseField, which relax() builds once and both the term and the scene's overlay share. Key L in QuadLayoutScene toggles the weight between 0 and 10 and rebuilds.

CreaseField radius floor: MINIMUM_RADIUS_EDGES = 3.0 average mesh edges, applied in build() as smoothingRadius = max(radius, floor). On fertility the asked-for radius is one quad edge = 2.258 = 1.02 mesh edges (a single Jacobi step); the floor lifts it to 6.613 = 3 edges, 9 steps, and the field goes from p95 0.4148 / max 1.140 (spiky) to p95 0.3245 / max 0.6735 (bands).

The load-bearing correction the first measurement forced: with the walk fixed at half a quad edge, the term did nothing. Half a quad edge on fertility is 1.13 mesh units — HALF an average mesh edge — and the crease field is now smoothed over 6.6, so the walk window was 6x narrower than the smoothing scale and saw a flat ramp, never a maximum. Measured: q mean 0.014, p95 0.058, and the site-to-target distance saturated exactly at 0.5*quadEdge for 95 percent of sites (the target was always the walk's far endpoint). Weight 10 and 30 then made the boundary-to-crease distance WORSE than weight 0 (0.512 and 0.565 against 0.484). Fix: the walk reach is now max(half a quad edge, CreaseField.smoothingRadius), in chart units chartReach = reach/quadEdgeLength, with the 3D travel cutoff kept as a safety and WALK_SAMPLES raised to 6. On fertility that is 6.613 = 3.08 quads. The rule is that the walk must reach at least as far as the bend was diffused, or the smoothing guarantees a flat window.

Fertility sweep (CreaseTermBenchmark, fertility_in_tri.off, alpha 15deg, 3378 boundary sites of which ~3300 carry a frozen triangle, walk reach 6.61 = 3.08 quads, q mean 0.08 / p95 0.33 / max 1.00). Boundary-to-crease distance before relaxation: mean 3.705, p95 6.249, max 6.606. After, by crease_weight: w=0 mean 3.183 p95 6.266, dirichlet 4.0197e4, coons 2.493e3, 1 pass, 49 it, 6.2s. w=1 mean 3.241 p95 6.144, dirichlet 4.0618e4 (+1.0%), coons 2.618e3, 3 passes, 72 it, 5.3s. w=3 mean 2.917 p95 5.981, dirichlet 4.1480e4 (+3.2%), coons 3.045e3, 3 passes, 87 it, 4.9s. w=10 mean 2.706 p95 5.828, dirichlet 4.3517e4 (+8.3%), coons 3.835e3, 3 passes, 120 it, 5.6s. w=30 mean 2.675 p95 6.003, dirichlet 4.5653e4 (+13.6%), coons 5.173e3, 3 passes, 160 it, 6.1s. flipped=0 at every weight. Recommended: w=10 — best p95 (-7.0% against weight 0), mean -15.0%, for +8.3% Dirichlet; w=30 buys almost no extra mean, loses the p95 gain and costs 13.6% distortion.

Overlay: the H key now also draws the pull vectors — one line per boundary site from its current position to its crease target, painted through the mesh_scalar thermal ramp by peakedness with the ramp at the sites' 95th percentile (QuadLayoutRuntime.setCreasePulls / creasePullRampMax, POSITION_SCALAR_LAYOUT drawn as GL_LINES at highlight width). Screenshots in the worktree's tmp/: patch-104-crease-weight0-legbase/-ridge/-waist.png against patch-104-crease-weight10-*.png (same cameras), plus patch-104-crease-pulls.png with the boundary and grid lines turned off so the pull field itself is legible. What moved at w=10: on the waist close-up the horizontal patch boundary that sat below the bright crease band at w=0 now runs along it, and the ring across the saddle below has climbed onto the neck; on the leg-base view every boundary ring on the trunk has migrated up toward the bright rim.
